shortcut_policy.preference: Use a qualified existing law and compatible measured data before deriving a replacement. Prefer structured tables/APIs/YAML/CellML/Modelica over AI extraction from prose.
adoption: Select the player-visible process and its accuracy/regime.
Pin raw data, model release, source terms and upstream tests.
Map units, species/grade, reference state, phase, orientation, history and frame.
Use the original implementation as an offline reference; choose direct native use or a compact qualified reduction.
Expose the same typed graph interface and validate composed behavior.
Reuse law-family qualification for additional in-envelope profiles; perform source/unit/range checks and a small representative regression per profile.
remaining_custom_work: Match identities and conditions across sources.
Choose sufficient state/history at the game's resolution.
Bind law outputs to geometry and paired exchanges.
Couple stiff laws and contacts without losing frequency/energy fidelity.
Measure runtime cost and player-visible accuracy.
Handle failure, topology, persistence and evidence freshness.
shortcut_policy.reference_vs_runtime: Modelica/FMUs, PyBaMM, FEBio and high-resolution Chrono models can be offline references. Model exchange/co-simulation does not automatically preserve stiff coupling, passivity or 300 Hz cost. Select explicit ownership, rollback and synchronization.
shortcut_policy.source_limits: Candidate routes are not newly downloaded or admitted parameter sets. Earlier pinned sources and their receipts remain exact historical records. Select and verify per-artifact licensing before distribution; do not presume one site's access policy applies to every contributed model.

state: phase, composition, damage and constitutive history only when required

ports.mechanical: Force/torque with conjugate velocity/angular velocity; work or impulse is owned and paired.
ports.thermal: Temperature and heat-flow rate; heat-flow rate itself has units of power.
ports.fluid: Pressure, composition and transported enthalpy with signed mass/species flow and momentum; do not count pressure-flow work twice when it is already in enthalpy.
ports.electrical: Voltage/current and charge state; V*I is electrical power.
ports.signal: Timestamped measured signal, latency and bandwidth; signal value is not a source of actuator energy.

common_interface.exchange: One exchange owner updates both participants atomically; external reservoirs and escaped mass, momentum and energy are explicit accounts. Port compatibility does not eliminate a simultaneous coupled solve.
common_interface.geometry: Mechanism definitions are not spatial instances. When instantiated, bind to versioned engine frames, regions, faces and oriented attachments. Graph layout/Gaussian presentation cannot stand in for physical coordinates.
common_interface.reduction: Lookup tables must preserve thermodynamic/constitutive consistency and relevant history. E(T), Cp(T) and p(U,V) cannot be independently interpolated into contradictory derivatives. Changing resolution conserves inventories and retains damage; it does not reconstruct unknown microstructure.

representative_composition.aluminum_hull: Grade-specific density + elastic/plastic/fracture profile + shell geometry + conductivity/expansion + spectral surface profile.
representative_composition.water: Same H2O identity, selected liquid/ice/vapor closure, latent energy, transport and interface-pair properties; solid mechanical response added for ice.
representative_composition.battery: An assembly of electrodes, electrolyte, separator and casing connected to electrochemical, electrical, thermal and failure laws.
representative_composition.muscle: Hydrated directional material + activation and force-length/velocity law + chemical supply + tendon attachment + delayed sensing.
representative_composition.rocket: Storage + finite nozzle outflow + energy conversion + exhaust momentum + free-body dynamics. The engine is an assembly, not a new material law.

source.operator.gpu_kernel_residency_202.name: Operator clarifies GPU matter kernel and smoothness target

document.text: Authored scope summary, not a verbatim transcript. The operator clarified that the teddy must work with Chimera's GPU-resident, Barnes-Hut-centered kernel system. Database properties become numerical matter state and interaction rules. The operator expects GPU residency to enable detailed physics and high-resolution rendering without stutter. This contract adopts residency and measured frame-time requirements; it does not assert that all physics follows inverse-square gravity or that residency alone proves zero stutter.

req.teddy_gpu_matter_kernel.name: Teddy uses resident GPU matter kernels and measured frame-time budgets

physical.statement: Implement teddy locomotion inside Chimera's GPU-resident, multi-kernel matter architecture.
physical.prediction: Source-derived material changes affect the same GPU state that produces motion and high-resolution rendering, within measured accuracy and performance limits.

contract.architecture: Database -> typed graph profile -> generated/admitted GPU law parameters -> resident matter state and spatial hierarchy -> field/local/constraint passes -> shared render snapshot.
contract.kernel_identity: Extend the existing multi-field Barnes-Hut/DSL architecture. Reuse existing membrane-port and articulated formulations as reference material for GPU integration; an independent external character simulator is not the accepted teddy runtime.

resident: mass, energy, composition and pressure state as required
local adjacency/contact data and constraint state
renderable geometry or GPU derivation inputs
residency.host: Graph provenance, source archives, compilation/admission, user commands and bounded asynchronous telemetry can remain on the host. GPU residency concerns the working simulation set, not fitting every scientific archive in VRAM.
residency.update: GPU tree build/refit or another qualified GPU hierarchy update, interaction evaluation, constraints, integration and rendering share versioned resident buffers with explicit synchronization.
residency.steady_state: No full-state CPU readback/reupload or CPU tree rebuild dependency per physics tick/frame. Telemetry/snapshots are separately budgeted asynchronous consumers.
residency.capacity: Declare VRAM working-set capacity, transient buffers and scene bounds. Preserve inventories and history during explicit LOD/streaming; never silently drop matter on overflow.

law_families.shared: Reuse spatial indexing, dispatch generation, reductions, typed exchanges, state ownership and render buffers.
law_families.far_field: Barnes-Hut aggregates eligible distant interactions under a per-kernel error criterion; nearby interactions descend or use a direct/local path.
law_families.local: Bonds, strain, pressure/volume constraints, contact/friction and joints use appropriate local adjacency/constraint passes on the same GPU state. A far-field monopole cannot substitute for local constitutive history or contact constraints.
law_families.physics: Gravity is one force law. Conservative mechanical forces can use F=-gradient(U); dissipation, actuator work and heat/species transport require explicit additional laws and accounts. Heat rate or a sampled scalar field is not automatically a force.
law_families.units: Every source coefficient declares units, frame, reference state and applicability; importing a float is not permission to reinterpret its dimension.

examples.gravity: U=-G*m_i*m_j/r under the selected point-mass approximation
examples.elastic_edge: U=0.5*k*(length-rest_length)^2 within the selected elastic model
examples.sealed_volume: U=(V-V0)^2/(2*kappa*V0) gives P=-(V-V0)/(kappa*V0) in the stated linear regime

law_families.spacetime: State evolves at physical time t over 3D spatial coordinates. Additional material channels are state dimensions; time does not become an ordinary octree distance coordinate.

mechanical_contract.ownership: One physical owner per degree of freedom; no duplicate masses or hidden pose writers.
mechanical_contract.attachment: Boundary force and moment enter the same body's momentum/constraint solve; skeleton and membrane exchanges work both ways.
mechanical_contract.reduction: Rigid or reduced bone models are permitted when their mass/inertia and boundary response represent the underlying material once.
mechanical_contract.controller: Balance/walking submit bounded intent or effort; actual motion follows solved forces, reactions and supplied energy.
mechanical_contract.external: MuJoCo/OpenSim and other simulators are data/reference sources or offline checks. Any borrowed numerical code must operate under the resident kernel's ownership and exchange contracts.

timing_and_quality.simulation: Fixed 300 Hz physical tick; choose coupled substeps from measured stiffness/frequency/contact error, independent of display cadence.
timing_and_quality.rendering: Render GPU-solved snapshots directly or interpolate consistently between them. Render resolution and physical refinement are separately budgeted.
timing_and_quality.target: Predictable frame delivery at declared scene, resolution, hardware and refresh rate. Zero stutter is an aspiration to test, not a consequence of residency alone.
scenarios: asset loading and cold shader compilation separately reported
timing_and_quality.accuracy: Do not conceal deadline misses by advancing less physical time, reducing contacts or changing stiffness without a declared LOD/fidelity change. Report backlog and resulting limits.

falsifier_controls: Disable routine CPU physics readback; walking and rendering must continue from resident state.
Change one admitted material parameter and observe its selected GPU law response without a second hand-maintained physics profile.
A boundary impulse changes total momentum and moment once; internal exchanges do not manufacture either.
Remove kernel contact support: the teddy can fall; no display-stage clamp or external simulator preserves support.
Compare near contacts and far-field approximation against direct/small reference cases with declared tolerances.
Test frame-time tails and missed deadlines while increasing detail; GPU residency alone cannot mark this performance test passed.
Pause kernel physical time: no separate walker continues advancing physical state.

source_inspection.method: read-only code inspection; no new runtime qualification
findings: kernel_dsl.py generates different per-quantity laws for one traversal, including outputs that are fields rather than forces.
spiace_phase6.html gpuBarnesHut builds/serializes a CPU tree, uploads particle arrays and maps readbacks each frame; that inspected prototype does not yet meet full residency.
Native joints.comp matter_step relaxes edges and clamps surface y; this alone does not establish momentum-accounted whole-body contact.
Existing Python articulated/floating models are candidate reusable formulations, not evidence of current native GPU teddy integration.

contract.status: Adopted architecture and acceptance requirements only. No GPU migration, new source import or walking implementation in this change.

gpu_force_channels.layout: A logical matrix/tensor of typed numerical channels indexed by stable physical entity IDs; GPU buffers may use structure-of-arrays packing. It need not be one dense N-by-N matrix of all pair interactions.
gpu_force_channels.coordinates: Spatial vectors use declared Cartesian engine/local frames, transforms and SI units. Gaussian coordinates here means the operator's spatial-coordinate concept; no Gaussian probability distribution is implied.

gravity.state: Mass and position plus selected field/source aggregates
gravity.mechanical_output: F=m*g, or qualified pair/tree gravitational force
gravity.scope: Uniform near-surface Earth g is a declared local reduction, not an extra force.

electromagnetism.state: E and B vectors where explicitly resolved; charge/current and constitutive material state as selected
electromagnetism.mechanical_output: q*(E+v cross B) for a selected particle model, or consistent effective continuum stress/force
electromagnetism.scope: Atomic-scale electromagnetic effects are usually represented by elasticity, contact, friction, transport and bonding laws. Avoid adding a second microscopic force to an already effective material response.

strong_nuclear.state: Selected isotope binding and evaluated reaction-channel data with product/energy inventory
strong_nuclear.scope: Game-scale reduced nuclear processes; not a universal long-range inverse-square field or a claim of QCD simulation.

weak_nuclear.state: Decay rates, branching and parent/daughter inventories with deposited/escaped energy
weak_nuclear.scope: Species/state transitions cannot be encoded only as a net force vector.

gpu_force_channels.conservation: Sum only compatible mechanical quantities in a common frame; keep energy and species exchanges in their own accounts. Forces are contributions evaluated from state, not sufficient independent state variables for every process.
gpu_force_channels.teddy_scope: Earth gravity and effective electromagnetic material/mechanical behavior are immediate. Nuclear descriptors are available as data categories and do not require nuclear updates for ordinary teddy walking.
gpu_force_channels.falsifier: A decay changes only velocity with no daughter/energy accounting, or heat/current is added numerically to force despite incompatible units.

lod_budget.priority: Use available GPU memory as the primary spatial/state-resolution budget. Compute, bandwidth and frame deadlines remain independent feasibility checks; fitting in VRAM does not by itself imply real-time performance.

target.actual_capacity: Query the actual selected adapter and per-heap budgets; do not hard-code the label as fully available simulation memory.

memory_source.semantics: heapBudget estimates total process allowance including existing allocations; heapUsage estimates existing process use. Budget can change with other applications and operating-system activity; it is not a guarantee.
memory_source.rule: For each relevant device-local heap, projected usage + explicitly reserved headroom must stay within current budget. Use projected allocation deltas for replacements; do not add existing usage twice.
memory_source.fallback: If dynamic budget queries are unsupported, record a conservative explicit budget and unknown availability; do not label nominal capacity as measured free VRAM.

accounting: cell volumes, inventory and constitutive history
tree nodes, leaf lists and per-kernel aggregates
render targets/textures/meshes in the same heap
transient peaks during tree rebuild, topology or LOD transitions
lod_budget.cost_model: B_total = sum(entity_count_i * measured_stride_i) + shared_tables + allocated_capacities + render_allocations + transition_peak; use actual allocator/heap observations to reconcile estimates. Count actual buffers once, including shared render/physics allocations only once.
lod_budget.representation: Measure bytes per active representation and its error/cost. A triangle references shared vertex, cell, material and attachment state; it need not duplicate all fields. Evaluate/reduce compatible force contributions rather than retaining a dense all-pairs force matrix. Keep history or individual interactions only where a selected law/solver requires them.
lod_budget.selection: Refine where local contacts, joint/membrane loads, deformation or field gradients demand accuracy. Coarsen eligible regions with declared reduced laws. Compare expected error improvement per additional byte while respecting measured compute cost.
lod_budget.conservation: Refinement/coarsening transfers mass, linear/angular momentum, energy, composition and damage/history consistently with the chosen representation. An irreversible cut or failure must not be erased by LOD.
lod_budget.stability: Preallocate bounded working pools where practical; budget old+new overlap during transitions, use hysteresis to avoid LOD oscillation, and preserve physically necessary contact/constraint detail. An over-budget state triggers explicit reduction/refusal, not silent paging as the routine physics path.
lod_budget.rendering: Physics resolution and pixel/visual mesh resolution are related but separately controlled. Higher display resolution consumes render memory and compute without necessarily requiring identical physical refinement.
telemetry: live versus reserved bytes by subsystem
selected physical LOD and error estimator
controls: Increase active detail until the declared budget boundary: adaptation/refusal occurs before knowingly exceeding reserved capacity.
Shrink the available budget while running: material inventories and damage survive the response.
Switch LOD repeatedly under a known load: force/work response stays within preregistered tolerance and no energy/material is manufactured.
Hold memory use fixed while increasing contacts: report solve-time limits instead of treating VRAM fit as proof of smoothness.

source.operator.creature_assembly_202609.name: Operator direction: reusable creature assembly, timed examples and planet interface

document.text: Codex synthesis of operator direction, not a verbatim transcript: The target is a coherent playable monkey built by reusable, graph-driven assembly of real-world data, material membranes and the resident GPU kernel. The same method must fit other humanoids. The selected monkey has hand-like feet and a tail; time-series primate motion examples should guide contact transitions, ground travel and climbing. Earth is a replaceable environment profile for the later space game. Repair disconnected body/skin behavior before training. Focus validation on changed behavior and integration gaps rather than rerunning familiar standalone demonstrations. The graph carries the method, data provenance, missing implementations and scoped proof; README remains the onboarding entrypoint.

physical.statement: Assemble the selected monkey and other humanoids through one versioned anatomy/material/binding contract.
physical.prediction: Every rendered vertex, physical boundary and anatomical attachment resolves to compatible source geometry and body state; changing a body profile does not require another handwritten physics system.

pipeline: scoped evidence returned to the graph
contract.identity: Stable graph IDs connect mesh vertices/faces, anatomical segments, compartments, joints, sensors and actuators. Engine spatial coordinates remain separate from graph roadmap layout.
contract.geometry: Canonical mesh checksum and vertex/topology ordering are required. World frame, handedness, length units, rest pose, pivot frames and joint axes are explicit. Two endpoint anchors need an explicit transverse direction to resolve roll. Mesh features are fitting observations, not a guarantee of internal anatomical centers.
contract.coverage: Every render component must have a declared mechanical attachment or independently simulated body, including eyes, face, tail and digits. A normalized skin weight is not proof of anatomical correctness, closed cells or coupled dynamics. Skeleton joints may drive descendants without directly owning vertices.
contract.ownership: One physical state owner. Rendering, pressure volumes, surface contacts and attachments read that state. Kinematic reference skinning does not qualify force-driven motion. Remove alternate pose writers from the accepted runtime path.
contract.membranes: A membrane identifies its oriented boundary and regions on both sides. Contact, bonding, sealing, sliding, permeability and signal transport are distinct connections. Spatial overlap never implies a bond; shared walls and material volume must not be counted twice.
contract.scaling: Fit segment lengths and frames to this asset; derive masses and inertias from its material geometry. Uniform geometric scaling s at fixed density gives mass s^3 and inertia s^5. Do not silently copy human strength, joint ranges or mass to the approximately 10-world-unit asset. Shape fitting is not biomechanical identification.
contract.effectors: Use capability-bearing endpoint sets rather than hardcoded two-foot support. The operator target has four grasp-capable extremities and a tail; actual digit count, joints, axes, limits and grip strength require explicit mapping. Tail balancing, support and prehensile gripping are separate capabilities.
contract.kernel: Use req.teddy_gpu_matter_kernel. Boundary triangles reference shared cell, material and body state; all interactions need not be inverse-square forces. Preserve mass, momentum, energy and history through LOD.
contract.motion_prerequisite: Begin control training only after body propagation, passive dynamics, bounded drives and contact limits are executable and checked.

current_asset.observation: Saved asset inspected, not live scene identity. Positions and topology exactly match this worktree engine snapshot. Named wrists/ankles and tail_base/mid/tip exist; separate finger/toe joints do not exist in this pack.

invalid bindings refuse without replacing prior state

contract.walking_climbing: Share the contact/actuator framework. Climbing introduces reachable grips, opposing contacts, hanging loads and different task/control requirements; walking success does not prove climbing. Tail curl alone does not establish a supporting contact.

remove active drive without freezing momentum

physical.statement: Use sourced temporal demonstrations and task outcomes to teach physically feasible movement on the selected morphology.

record_schema: body model and semantic joint IDs
original timestamps or verified sampling interval

contract.goal_window: Specify a range of acceptable final configurations plus support/contact state, bounded velocity and a dwell interval. Reaching one visually similar frame while falling is not success. Task completion and physical feasibility are evaluated independently of imitation score.
contract.reward: Use normalized pose/velocity/contact-phase errors or a learned motion prior as a hint, plus task progress and effort costs. Weights are declared control-design choices, not measured material constants. Force, friction, joint range and energy bounds are enforced by dynamics, not traded away through reward weights.
contract.retarget: Map shared anatomical functions and endpoint contacts, fit scale/frames, solve constrained motion retargeting, then train on the actual monkey morphology. Preserve unmatched digits/tail as unresolved. Human examples can help shared skills but do not supply monkey grip mechanics.
contract.time: Keep physical timestamps and a separate normalized phase. Interpolation to 300 Hz is not 300 Hz measured data. Report gaps, smoothing and derivative uncertainty. Time warping changes required velocity and acceleration; enforce dynamic feasibility after retiming.
curriculum: tail assistance only when supported by explicit mechanics
contract.evaluation: Split by recording/episode and subject where appropriate, not adjacent frames. Include held-out supports, disturbances, invalid grips, slipping and power loss. A trained policy must still run under the actual kernel resource/accuracy limits.

document.text: Codex synthesis, not a verbatim transcript: The operator requests a scan-derived, layered anatomical reference containing bone, ligament, tendon, muscle, fat, skin and sensory structures, so membranes within membranes can build reusable living-looking game organisms. Human anatomy is a reference for fitting the selected monkey and other humanoid forms. No exposed genital anatomy or sexual simulation is required. Eyes and ears must provide sensory observations driving behavior, not only appearance. The continuing goal is an integrated physical creature in a space game.

The 99% archive denotes polygon reduction, not 99% retained detail.

req.layered_anatomy.name: Layered anatomical reference fitted into reusable membrane bodies

physical.statement: Use identified anatomical geometry plus separately sourced constitutive, actuator and sensor models to assemble the game body.
physical.prediction: A force applied to skin can pass through compliant tissues and attachments to the skeleton; sensory observations can cause bounded, delayed actuator responses through that same body.

pipeline: pin anatomy identities, part membership and mesh/scan artifacts
segment where needed and validate frame, scale, topology and coverage
fit articulated anatomy to the target mesh with explicit human-to-creature mappings
assign bulk regions, boundary membranes and sliding/bonded/transport interfaces
source tissue and actuator parameters with units, conditions and uncertainty
compile selected model fidelity into existing resident kernel buffers
drive and sense the single physical state used for rendering and contact

layers.representation: Cortical/trabecular regions as rigid or elastic segments at selected fidelity; boundaries and attachment sites.
layers.limit: A sealed bone compartment is not a water-filled bag by default.

layers.representation: Articular surfaces, unilateral contact/sliding and capsular constraints; optional fluid region with a declared law.
Tension-bearing paths/regions with insertions, slack, wrapping and strain-dependent response.
Finite-volume contractile regions or reduced muscle-tendon actuators; activation changes active tension within force, rate and energy limits.
layers.limit: A muscle surface mesh alone does not determine its fiber architecture or motor control.

layers.representation: Compliant bulk plus enclosing/contact surfaces; declared attachments permit appropriate sliding and transmit pressure/shear.
required_data: boundary tension or prestress where applicable
layers.limit: A single surface-tension scalar does not specify all solid mechanics.

layers.representation: Eyes, ears, skin receptors, joint sensing and balance observations use req.embodied_senses.
Anatomical geometry/mass can be present while function is reduced to explicit storage, pressure, flow, power or thermal variables according to gameplay.
layers.limit: Heart, lung or gut meshes do not require cellular simulation to supply game-scale effects; omitted physiology stays labeled.

contract.boundaries: Bodies contain regions as well as surfaces. A shared interface has two sides and one accounted physical interaction. Compartment nesting and sliding/bonding are explicit; overlapping reference meshes are not automatically valid nested sealed cells.
contract.energy: Account for actuator work and passive storage/dissipation. Muscle activation is not free injected motion. Parameters for density, stiffness, viscosity, strength and active tension remain distinct even when their contributions enter the same momentum update.
contract.data_joins: Use source release, FMA/other anatomy identity, laterality, specimen, frame and representation identity. IS-A is classification; PART-OF is anatomy membership; neither creates a physical bond. Missing tissue is an explicit gap, not silently filled by a guessed dataset match.
contract.lod: Separate visible surface resolution, mechanical resolution and control/sensor update rates. Preserve masses, inertias, attachments and declared conservation when reducing detail; 24 GB capacity alone does not guarantee frame time.
contract.product_subset: No exposed genital geometry or sexual simulation. Preserve the raw scientific sources and make game export an explicit subset. Keep the selected monkey as the first integrated target; a human reference is not a species-identical physical calibration.
contract.build_order: Finish one shared render/contact/hydraulic body state, then exercise a complete skin-fat-muscle-tendon-bone limb chain on that body and add causal sensing. Expand anatomy by the same assembly contract; importing the full atlas is not a prerequisite for resolving the current ownership defect.
contract.completion: One coherent creature supports pressing, delayed response, force-limited motion and loss of support; a second morphology uses the same assembly. Anatomical completeness and validated physiological fidelity are reported separately.

falsifier.statement: A body whose muscles move its appearance but cannot transmit loads through tendons into bone is not mechanically assembled.

req.embodied_senses.name: Embodied visual, auditory, touch and balance observations

physical.statement: Sensory structures produce observations from the simulated world, through finite-rate and delayed signal routes into the creature controller.
physical.prediction: Occluding a visual target, removing a sound, or cutting one signal route changes the matching active response while unrelated passive mechanics remains available.

contract.vision: Attach bounded field-of-view cameras or ray/depth/color sensors to eye frames. Respect orientation, occlusion, lighting assumptions, sample rate, noise and latency. Track only observed targets; no hidden unrestricted target pose input. Full retinal chemistry and conscious perception are outside the qualified game model.
contract.hearing: Attach paired receivers to the head with a declared sound propagation/occlusion approximation, local-medium speed and level/direction observations. Distance/speed contributes arrival delay. Disable airborne transmission in a declared vacuum while separately modeled structural contact sound may remain. A visual ear mesh does not supply hearing.
contract.touch: Local pressure, deformation and slip measurements on physical boundary patches, with calibrated thresholds, sampling and signal delays; no global omniscient damage trigger masquerading as local sensation.
contract.proprioception_and_balance: Observe joint angle/rate/load and body orientation/angular velocity/specific force through declared sensor models. These are required for the control problem even when the inner-ear geometry is not resolved.
contract.pathways: Stable sender/receiver IDs, finite delay, ordering and cuttable connectivity. Delays use simulation time, not render cadence or Internet time. Preserve pending signal state across supported save/restore.
controls: occluded target does not generate a new unobserved visual measurement
identical sound moved left/right changes paired observations consistently
airborne sound disappears under the vacuum boundary model
cut sensory route removes that active response without freezing passive motion
remove or delay balance observations and measure the controller consequence separately from mechanical stability

contract.prompt:
You are starting a new Z Code / GLM 5.3 session with zero conversation context. The project home is E:\PythonChimera. E:\Chimera is the older project. Start at README.md in the current assigned checkout. The last development lane was E:\ChimeraWork\codex-graph-workflow-20260916 on codex/force-data-runtime-20260916; verify its current state before using it. The project home has a separate historical, dirty detached checkout: do not reset it or assume it is the published tree.

GOAL AND METHOD
Build an integrated macaque for a physical space game: pinned scientific/anatomical data -> typed graph -> reusable material/anatomy/force components -> native kernel -> visible physical interaction -> scoped evidence. The graph holds the active documentation, roadmap, sources, laws and observations. Graphify is a checked projection of the selected authority. The README is the only onboarding entrypoint. A source import is not runtime proof; a test pass does not qualify the whole creature.

START HERE
1. Follow README checkout checks: repository/common git directory, branch, HEAD, dirty state and remote. Preserve others' changes and running worlds.
2. Run project_spec --check; read req.agent_operation, req.publication_workflow, req.current_product_focus, req.macaque_rebuild and this doc.handoff.zcode from the selected graph.
3. Read doc.workflow.macaque_assembly, doc.workflow.earth_patch, doc.workflow.force_arm, doc.workflow.coupled_arm and doc.workflow.coupled_native. Follow their exact scoped receipts and source hashes. Do not replay unchanged demonstrations just to manufacture activity.
4. Inspect controller/session availability. Use only your provisioned credentials. Explicitly authorized isolated repository work may proceed without controller admission; do not invent enrollment or restart shared services.

CURRENT TRUTH
The pinned MIT macaque arm model contains seven metric bone meshes, seven joint coordinates and 39 musculotendon records. It is a research segment model, not a certified full-body scan. Source topology gaps, conditional muscle points and wrapping semantics remain visible.
The Earth interface uses pinned NGA/JPL/NASA inputs and existing kernel laws for gravity, atmosphere, contact and heat. Procedural ground is not surveyed terrain. doc.workflow.earth_patch has its qualified scope.
The native force-arm example drives one physical elbow with source inertia, finite ideal actuator work, gravity and unilateral hand support. It can fall, stall and exert reactions. Its receipt covers 19 native, 25 live, 21 Python, 23 existing-Earth and 7 Graphify checks plus browser review. The actual angle is not a target pose write. energy.battery_usable controls depletion display. Read the receipt instead of inferring full-body or biological fidelity.
The new coupled-arm Python reference derives M(q), gravity, velocity-dependent bias and point-force Jacobians for the seven source coordinates. Its ten independent tests include analytic two-link dynamics, FK kinetic energy/gravity/acceleration, virtual work and the existing elbow inertia. It does not integrate the seven coordinates in the native engine. Its scoped receipt is tools/science_funnel/validation/coupled_arm_20260917/receipt.json. Seven numeric reference cases and their safe scratch-output replay support native parity. Read the observation/receipt before claiming qualification.
A native two-coordinate shoulder/elbow reference is now implemented at /earth on a private 8127 scene: model.dynamics.coupled_arm and doc.workflow.coupled_native. It has finite ideal actuator energy, source joint stops and a hand-applied force, with no environment collision. Read tools/science_funnel/validation/coupled_native_20260917/receipt.json for the exact qualified candidate and limits. Free-root balance, actual muscles, watertight bone/tissue layers, a whole macaque and GPU-resident multibody dynamics remain unfinished. Neither biological movement nor whole-creature aliveness may be claimed from these references.

NEXT EXECUTABLE WORK
Read work.creature.coupled_arm_native and doc.workflow.coupled_native for the two-coordinate implementation and its exact checks. Continue with the missing hand/environment contact gap and Jacobian, coupled reactions and friction; preserve cross-joint inertia/bias and work accounts. The scalar arm's angle-based support cannot serve as a two-coordinate collision solver. Derive a contact gap/Jacobian and reaction impulses, or explicitly scope contact out of the first free-motion qualification. Never silently clip poses or regularize missing mass.
Independent scopes already exist: work.creature.macaque_whole_body_sources, work.creature.macaque_bone_boundaries, work.creature.macaque_muscle_paths and work.environment.terrain. Reuse current imports instead of rebuilding them. Preserve licenses, checksums, units, species/specimen qualifiers, source resolution, holes and unknown parameters.

PARALLEL WORK, SERIAL INTEGRATION
Use subagents explicitly, up to ten when ten useful independent tasks and actual host capacity exist. Verify the configured parent/subagent models; use GLM 5.3 Flash only if the host actually routes workers there. Give each worker a graph work ID, exact base/input identities, prediction, falsifier, owned files and private build/output directory. No two workers edit a shared native interface or graph concurrently. Declarations, definitions and callers land as one coherent change through one serial integrator.
Checkpoint task ID, base revision, files, last completed command, failures and next action so dead workers can be resumed. Confirm old execution stopped before assigning its scope elsewhere. Never let worker keep-alive failures become an invisible stall. Complex native work belongs in a concrete senior/Codex packet; keep independent implementation/source/evidence work moving while it waits.

PROOF AND PUBLICATION
Freeze a coherent candidate; run only checks relevant to actual changes. Keep failures, source identities and runtime scope. Record observations through validated graph APIs; only the authorized verifier promotes gates. Eleven historical evidence records must remain unchanged. Runtime graph snapshots keep their compiled identity when documentation advances.
The operator has explicitly authorized routine publication to the existing GhostDragonAlpha/Chimera GitHub repository, including the assigned branch and authorized master integration. The two-coordinate native candidate 9ab72288df8ea966d4edb4864c95975f04e1d810 was verified on both branch and master; its proof is in the coupled_native receipt. Read current refs; publish completed commits promptly, non-forcibly, and verify remote tips. Do not repeat the earlier permission request merely because a handoff was stale. Follow any actual tool rejection without bypassing it.
Maintain README bootstrap and this graph handoff after meaningful changes. End each bounded assignment with changed behavior, exact candidate/receipt, qualified scope, actual blockers and the next executable work. Do not declare the engine or whole project finished.

physical.statement: A pinned MIT macaque upper-limb model supplies real metric geometry, source joint frames and explicit musculotendon records.
physical.prediction: Compiled native vertices match the source transform model within 0.2 micrometres at rest and two mixed joint configurations; all bone edge lengths remain unchanged within that tolerance.

contract.source_class: Published research-model geometry, not certified specimen scans; species/specimen and original mesh ancestry unresolved. Effective segment mass must not be assigned as bone mass.
pipeline: parse_source verifies every upstream file hash and MIT license identity
strict OpenSim 3 adapter preserves SI frames, coordinate limits, path/wrap/conditional records
build_proposal creates source, body, geometry and muscle objects with explicit graph connections
compile_native reads graph model and pinned geometry into metre-scale mesh and JNT3 hierarchy
private launcher uses topology-preserving native upload and the existing game shell
native poses are compared against the source-frame oracle through the viewer API
contract.runtime_policy: Choose free private ports. Default private artifacts .tmp/macaque-anatomy; engine .tmp/anatomy-engine. Never replace a running creature. No water seals are requested. Viewer refuses unqualified bone touch/gravity; direct engine APIs remain general-purpose, not an anatomical material sandbox.
contract.geometry_processing: Exact-coordinate welding plus source-to-render vertex map and concave polygon triangulation. One zero-area radius polygon omitted explicitly. No source point moved and no hole capped.
contract.topology: Scapula has 10 edges and hand 18 edges not shared by exactly two triangles; remain unqualified for sealing. The other five pass edge-incidence checks, which alone do not certify oriented manifold, connectedness or lack of self-intersection.
contract.native_scope: Kinematic geometry; source limits include shoulder adduction below -90 degrees. No force-driven muscle, whole animal, skin/fat geometry or locomotion claim.

counts.browser: Actual elbow slider plus ArrowRight, source-frame vertex oracle, reset button, no browser errors; canvas owner native.

observation.scope: Pinned macaque upper-limb source geometry and parameters -> connected graph objects -> metric native kinematic assembly -> same streamed viewer geometry. No requirement statuses advanced.

preregistered_failures: native/source pose or bone edge error exceeds 2e-7 m
compiled source triangle indices change in streamed topology
any wrap/conditional semantics discarded or promoted to ready actuator
rebuild or Graphify projection loses objects/relations

work.creature.macaque_bone_boundaries.name: Repair and qualify bone boundaries without inventing scan evidence

physical.statement: Open or non-manifold source display geometry cannot become a sealed physical cell through visual inspection alone.
physical.prediction: Repair records preserve the source artifact, identify changed faces and newly inferred patches, and qualify orientation, edge incidence, signed volume and intersections before any sealed-layer claim.

contract.method: Diagnose duplicate/coincident faces and connected components first. Preserve original vertices where possible. Any new patch is derived repair geometry, not source anatomy. Check all seven bone surfaces, not just currently flagged edge incidence.
contract.runtime: Do not run water law on bones; separate solid constitutive state and tissue interfaces are required.

falsifier.statement: A boundary that cannot disclose its inferred patches cannot be called a measured sealed bone.

work.creature.macaque_muscle_paths.name: Resolve source muscle wrapping before force-driven actuation

physical.statement: Thirty source muscle records use wrapping surfaces and one path point is conditional; anchors alone do not define their moving lengths.
physical.prediction: Resolved paths obey source wrap geometry and conditional ranges, and finite-difference path-length derivatives agree with moment arms before activation can produce torque.

contract.method: Implement supported wrapping per source semantics; refuse unsupported geometry. Preserve source curves and modeling assumptions. Measure continuity across contact changes; apply equal and opposite attachment forces and account for work. Native constraint/actuator implementation remains Codex-owned.
falsifiers: path enters a wrapping obstacle
discontinuous length when the physical path should be continuous
moment arm differs from -dL/dq beyond declared error
nonzero force from inactive unsupported model
unaccounted net force/work

falsifier.statement: A muscle that cannot transmit and account for mechanical work cannot move the skeleton honestly.

contract.coordinates: Global datum and ECEF origin in float64; local right-handed X east, Y up, Z south in metres. Render local coordinates, never subtract planet-scale float32 positions to recover millimetres.

terrain surface with collision, friction and constitutive material

contract.interface: sample_fields(position,simulation_time) plus explicit boundary contacts and impulse/heat/mass/signal exchange records. A field value is not itself a force; body properties and interaction law determine the exchange.
contract.accounting: Environment reservoirs have explicit reaction impulse, transferred heat and work. Static ground and prescribed wind are reservoirs, not hidden infinite-energy creature actuators. Configuration changes start new trials until transitions have a physical work/mass accounting law.
contract.resolution: Planet DEMs resolve regional shape; near-contact ground needs independently justified smaller-scale geometry/material data. Upsampling a coarse DEM does not create measured foot-contact detail. LOD must preserve mass/inertia, energy and boundary identity.

data_routes.surface_materials: measured pairwise friction, moisture, compliance, roughness; unknown until sourced

data_routes.sunlight: ephemeris and radiometry; not an arbitrary heat source

contract.body_independent_interface: chimera::environment::sample_earth(Library, parameters, latitude, longitude, altitude, air) returns a float64 frame, central acceleration in ECEF, gravity magnitude, pressure, temperature and density. Body-specific interactions consume this sample. Local reference uses central magnitude along local up; full rotating-Earth dynamics remain unimplemented.

operators.gravity: Existing Library::gravity uses pinned JPL Earth GM; exact constant-acceleration local flight with analytic impact time. Metre-scale patch freezes gravity and air at its anchor.
operators.drag: Exact fixed-wind subflow u_new=u/(1+k|u|dt/m); k=0.5 rho Cd A. Wind work w dot impulse and nonnegative relative kinetic loss are separate.
operators.buoyancy: rho_air V g upward for the closed reference cell; atmospheric reservoir work equals rho V g delta_y.
operators.contact: Analytic plane intersection; perfectly inelastic normal impulse; Coulomb tangential impulse and constrained sliding with a static threshold. No rolling or distributed foot pressure.
operators.thermal: Lumped Newton heat transfer T_new=T_air+(T-T_air)exp(-h A dt/C). Heat ledger is exactly C(T_old-T_new). These lumped coefficients are authored reference assumptions.

exchange_ports: air drag and buoyancy reaction impulse
ground heat from friction and impact
air heat from convective exchange and drag dissipation
wind work and buoyancy reservoir work
contract.physics_clock: 300 Hz native monotonic-clock worker; simulation time = tick count / 300, separate from render rate and wall/Internet time. Explicit reset creates a new epoch. Clock lag remains visible.
contract.controls: Release begins a trial from a kinematic hand attachment. Pose and environment controls reset preparation state explicitly; no dynamic biological grasp or infinite-strength servo claim. Environment configuration is transactional and unknown/duplicate controls refuse.
contract.geometry: Same admitted metre-scale arm hierarchy; a prescribed local shoulder mount; authored 2.4 m rigid plane; analytic support sphere displayed by inscribed triangles. Graph source axes remain distinct from roadmap layout.
contract.energy_partition: All mechanical contact/friction loss goes to the ground reservoir; relative-air drag loss goes to air. Convective heat can flow either direction. This reference does not add impact heat to the sample. Total accounts expose residuals, not automatic truth assertions.
contract.data_limits: NGA WGS84 shape/frame and JPL central gravity; NASA historical educational atmosphere fit restricted to 0–10 km. Not weather or a modern full standard-atmosphere implementation. Preserve NASA 273.1 curve-fit offset separately from Celsius/Kelvin conversion. Friction, Cd, mass and thermal coefficients are author-specified, not laboratory measurements of a seed, bone or soil.

derivation: For each body downstream of the elbow, transform its COM inertia into the reference frame and shift to the elbow: I_h=sum(R I_C R^T + m((r dot r)1-r r^T)).
Scalar inertia is a^T I_h a; COM first moment S=sum(m r). Rotating S determines gravity potential and torque. Fixed upstream mass is excluded from elbow inertia.
Map a hand normal force by virtual work: tau=J_y F_y, J_y=(a cross R(q) r_hand)_y.
Energy-conserving discrete gradient: q1-q0=h(w0+w1)/2; I(w1-w0)=h(tau-Ubar_prime-b(w0+w1)/2). Ubar_prime=[U(q1)-U(q0)]/(q1-q0), evaluated with sinc to avoid cancellation.
Locate boundary impact within the tick, lose exactly I w_hit^2/2 for zero restitution, then integrate or support the remaining interval. No arbitrary pose clamp.
Limit positive motor work to available stored energy; record named exhaustion and passive continuation.

contract.source_interpretation: OpenSim Body inertia is about its center of mass, expressed in the body frame. The existing MIT-pinned macaque source supplies effective segment values, including its tiny regularization body. Preserve them and their ancestry; never treat them as isolated visible bone density.
contract.source_reduction: tools/science_funnel/force_arm.py derives downstream membership, first mass moment and composite inertia tensor by frame transformation and the parallel-axis theorem. The one-axis inertia is .0019939687829337097 kg m^2 and moving mass .203001 kg for this exact admitted source. Source FK finite differences provide an independent kinetic-energy and gravity-gradient oracle.
contract.dynamic_owner: ChimeraEngine/engine/arm_dynamics.hpp owns q, speed, motor energy and impulse/work history. GraphEarth maps the solved q into the existing source binding. Controller target changes never directly write q. Initialization/reset is explicitly separate.
contract.integration: Fixed native 300 Hz. A unique bracketed discrete-gradient solve closes work and energy. Its sufficient residual monotonicity condition is 2I/h^2+b/h > (gravity+load potential amplitude)/2. Analytic potential divided differences use sinc. Locate hard-boundary impacts within each tick; zero restitution loses I*w_hit^2/2; residual interval is integrated or supported. Time refinement has a separate native check; conservation alone does not establish accuracy.
contract.actuator: Authored ideal torque-capped position/velocity feedback. kp=I*(2*pi*f)^2, kd=2*zeta*I*(2*pi*f), passive b=I*decay_rate. No empirical motor or muscle force-velocity claim. Positive discrete work consumes a finite mechanical store; negative work becomes brake heat. There is no isometric metabolic/electrical cost.
contract.exhaustion: Solve for the largest affordable effort against actual solved displacement. Battery never negative; <=1e-12 J is retained as unusable numerical remainder and triggers a named exhaustion event. No silent refilling except explicit Reset trial. Native energy.battery_usable is the authoritative availability flag; the viewer must not infer availability from rounded joules or exact-zero comparisons.
contract.contact: Orange hand proxy is rigidly attached at the admitted source-hand centroid with the existing25mm offset defined in the rest pose. The support is a unilateral horizontal plane at the configured80deg elbow pose minus proxy radius. Positive height Jacobian is required over the admitted source range. Bone mesh collision, distributed palm pressure and grasp are not qualified.

accounts.force: For the moving distal assembly, mount impulse = change of linear momentum - gravity impulse - applied hand-load impulse - support impulse. The fixed upper-arm own weight is outside this reduced reaction account.
accounts.signs: load_N is downward at hand; positive support reaction is upward. Motor reaction torque on the fixed upstream assembly is the opposite applied motor effort.

contract.controls: target_deg, power, torque_limit_N_m and load_N are force intents. Support changes require reset:true. paused freezes physical time. Legacy elbow_deg pose writes are refused in this mode.
visible_falsifiers: Cut power: active work becomes zero but the arm still falls.
Reduce effort: actual angle misses the target.
Demand a blocked angle: angle stops and support force remains measurable.
Exhaust stored energy: positive active work stops and passive motion remains.

contract.goal: Two native source-derived coordinates drive the same visible anatomical chain. Force intent replaces angle writes; coupled inertia, gravity, bias and work determine motion.
derivation: M=sum(m Jv^T Jv + Jw^T R I_COM R^T Jw); generalized gravity=sum(Jv^T m g). Analytic first and directional second source-transform derivatives yield inertial bias.
M qdd=tau+J_hand^T F+gravity-bias-B qdot+constraint reactions. Source inertia is effective segment inertia, not visible bone material.

Joint stops use admissible-velocity projection in inverse-M metric; nonnegative unilateral impulses dissipate kinetic energy. Event-localized crossing splits a substep. Supporting reactions use the same active-set mass matrix.
Four RK4 substeps per fixed 300 Hz tick. Capped effort held per substep; actuator work=tau dot delta_q. Downward-load work=-F delta_hand_y. Viscous loss uses RK4 quadrature.

Positive net work per actuator per substep consumes the 2 J mechanical store. Negative net actuator work becomes brake heat. Effort is scaled when a trial exceeds available energy; no regeneration or metabolic claim.
Energy measured relative to reset pose: delta(K+U)=W_drive+W_external-Q_damping-Q_impacts. Combined store balance includes brake heat.
contract.controls: Targets and torque limits are intent only. Both drive switches and global power gate effort. Reset retains controls, resets q/qdot and restores 2 J. Pause freezes integration. Unknown/direct-pose controls refuse transactionally.
contract.qualification: Scoped candidate 9ab72288df8ea966d4edb4864c95975f04e1d810 checked; exact results and limitations: tools/science_funnel/validation/coupled_native_20260917/receipt.json. No production gate promotion.
numerical_limits: RK4 explicit reference is qualified only for this source model, admitted gains/caps and timestep; no unconditional stability claim. Endpoint crossing/event bisection is not a general arbitrary-speed continuous collision detector.
Worst energy/store residual must remain below 1e-5 J on preregistered ten-second trials. Free trajectory refinement must approach fourth order; impact trajectories require their own event tolerances.
CPU reference, two coordinates. Native analytic force snapshots support all seven source coordinates; seven-coordinate trajectories are not qualified.

Work consumption and braking are resolved per substep; within-substep reversals are not separately metered. The energy ledger is a discrete ideal-work model. Earth air/temperature fields are informational here; only sampled gravity enters arm dynamics.
contract.next: Derive hand-environment signed gap and two-coordinate contact Jacobian, solve nonnegative impulses with friction and separate reaction/energy oracles. Do not reuse scalar elbow-angle support. Then free-root balance after whole-body inertias and contacts are available.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0000144.definition: The medial portion of the articular surface of the humerus is named the trochlea, and presents a deep depression between two well-marked borders; it is convex from before backward, concave from side to side, and occupies the anterior, lower, and posterior parts of the extremity. ref.uberon.UBERON_0001010.name: diaphysis of ulna
ref.uberon.UBERON_0001010.definition: The body of the ulna at its upper part is prismatic in form, and curved so as to be convex behind and lateralward; its central part is straight; its lower part is rounded, smooth, and bent a little lateralward. It tapers gradually from above downward, and has three borders and three surfaces.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0001012.name: head of radius
ref.uberon.UBERON_0001012.definition: The head of the radius has a cylindrical form, and on its upper surface is a shallow cup or fovea for articulation with the capitulum (or capitellum) of the humerus. The circumference of the head is smooth; it is broad medially where it articulates with the radial notch of the ulna, narrow in the rest of its extent, which is embraced by the annular ligament. The deepest point in the fovea is not axi-symmetric with the long axis of the radius, creating a cam effect during pronation and supination[WP].

ref.uberon.UBERON_0001269.name: acetabular part of hip bone
ref.uberon.UBERON_0001269.definition: The acetabulum is a concave surface of the pelvis. The head of the femur meets with the pelvis at the acetabulum, forming the hip joint. There are three bones of the os coxae (hip bone) that come together to form the acetabulum. Contributing a little more than two-fifths of the structure is the ischium, which provides lower and side boundaries to the acetabulum. The ilium forms the upper boundary, providing a little less than two-fifths of the structure of the acetabulum. The rest is formed by the pubis, near the midline. It is bounded by a prominent uneven rim, which is thick and strong above, and serves for the attachment of the acetabular labrum, which reduces its opening, and deepens the surface for formation of the hip joint. At the lower part of the acetabulum is the acetabular notch, which is continuous with a circular depression, the acetabular fossa, at the bottom of the cavity of the acetabulum. The rest of the acetabulum is formed by a curved, crescent-moon shaped surface, the lunate surface, where the joint is made with the head of the femur. Its counterpart in the pectoral girdle is the glenoid fossa.[WP,unvetted].
ref.uberon.UBERON_0001269.notes: EXTRACTED: Uberon states it; not a creature part, not physically verified. Human anatomy is REFERENCE, never automatically Chimera proportions.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0001272.name: innominate bone
ref.uberon.UBERON_0001272.definition: A fused bone consisting of the ilium, ischium and pubis. Together with the sacrum and coccyx, it comprises the pelvis. [WP,modified].
ref.uberon.UBERON_0001272.notes: EXTRACTED: Uberon states it; not a creature part, not physically verified. Human anatomy is REFERENCE, never automatically Chimera proportions.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0001273.name: ilium
ref.uberon.UBERON_0001273.definition: Paired endochondral bone that is the dorsal-most of the pelvic bones, offering attachment areas for gluteal muscles on its main surface [PHENOSCAPE:ad].

ref.uberon.UBERON_0002495.name: long bone
ref.uberon.UBERON_0002495.definition: "A long bone is a bone that has a shaft and 2 ends and is longer than it is wide. Long bones have a thick outside layer of compact bone and an inner medullary cavity containing bone marrow.  The ends of a long bone contain spongy bone and an epiphyseal plate or line depending on the stage of development. The epiphyseal plate is a hyaline cartilage, where new bone growth takes place, lengthening the bone prior to adulthood. Bone lengthening ceases when this cartilage is lost, leaving a remnant referred to as an epiphyseal line." [https://medlineplus.gov/ency/imagepages/9582.htm, Wikipedia:Long_bone] {seeAlso="https://github.com/obophenotype/uberon/issues/32", seeAlso="https://github.com/obophenotype/uberon/issues/2010"}

It is directed a little lateralward and backward, and, in the adult, is about 1 cm lower than the head. Because the pelvic outlet in the female is larger than in the male, there is a greater distance between the greater trochanters in the female. It has two surfaces and four borders. [WP,unvetted].

ref.uberon.UBERON_0006767.name: head of femur
ref.uberon.UBERON_0006767.definition: The hemispheric articular surface at the upper extremity of the thigh bone[Stedman, 26th ed]. The femur head is the highest part of the thigh bone. It is supported by the neck of the femur. The head is globular and forms rather more than a hemisphere, is directed upward, medialward, and a little forward, the greater part of its convexity being above and in front. Its surface is smooth, coated with cartilage in the fresh state, except over an ovoid depression, the fovea capitis femoris, which is situated a little below and behind the center of the head, and gives attachment to the ligament of head of femur. If there is a fracture of the neck of the femur, the blood supply through the ligament becomes crucial. In orthopedic surgery, the head of the femur is important because it can undergo avascular necrosis and consequent osteochondritis dissecans. The head is removed in total hip replacement surgery [WP].

ref.uberon.UBERON_0006810.name: olecranon
ref.uberon.UBERON_0006810.definition: The olecranon is a large, thick, curved bony eminence of the forearm that projects behind the elbow. It is situated at the upper (proximal) end of the ulna, one of the two bones in the forearm. When the hand faces forward the olecranon faces towards the back (posteriorly). It is bent forward at the summit so as to present a prominent lip which is received into the olecranon fossa of the humerus in extension of the forearm. Its base is contracted where it joins the body and the narrowest part of the upper end of the ulna. Its posterior surface, directed backward, is triangular, smooth, subcutaneous, and covered by a bursa. Its superior surface is of quadrilateral form, marked behind by a rough impression for the insertion of the Triceps brachii; and in front, near the margin, by a slight transverse groove for the attachment of part of the posterior ligament of the elbow-joint. Its anterior surface is smooth, concave, and forms the upper part of the semilunar notch. Its borders present continuations of the groove on the margin of the superior surface; they serve for the attachment of ligaments, viz. , the back part of the ulnar collateral ligament medially, and the posterior ligament laterally. From the medial border a part of the Flexor carpi ulnaris arises; while to the lateral border the anconeus muscle is attached.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0007173.name: lateral border of scapula
ref.uberon.UBERON_0007173.definition: The lateral border (or axillary border, or margin) is the thickest of the three borders of the scapula. It begins above at the lower margin of the glenoid cavity, and inclines obliquely downward and backward to the inferior angle. Immediately below the glenoid cavity is a rough impression, the infraglenoid tuberosity, about 2.5 cm. in length, which gives origin to the long head of the Triceps brachii; in front of this is a longitudinal groove, which extends as far as the lower third of this border, and affords origin to part of the Subscapularis. The inferior third is thin and sharp, and serves for the attachment of a few fibers of the Teres major behind, and of the Subscapularis in front.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0007174.name: medial border of scapula
ref.uberon.UBERON_0007174.definition: The medial border of the scapula (vertebral border, medial margin) is the longest of the three borders, and extends from the medial to the inferior angle. It is arched, intermediate in thickness between the superior and the axillary borders, and the portion of it above the spine forms an obtuse angle with the part below. This border presents an anterior and a posterior lip, and an intermediate narrow area. The anterior lip affords attachment to the Serratus anterior; the posterior lip, to the Supraspinatus above the spine, the Infraspinatus below; the area between the two lips, to the Levator scapulC& above the triangular surface at the commencement of the spine, to the Rhomboideus minor on the edge of that surface, and to the Rhomboideus major below it; this last is attached by means of a fibrous arch, connected above to the lower part of the triangular surface at the base of the spine, and below to the lower part of the border.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0007831.name: pectoral girdle skeleton
ref.uberon.UBERON_0007831.definition: A subdivision of a limb or fin skeleton consisting of bones which connects the upper limb or fin to the axial skeleton on each side. It consists of the clavicle and scapula in humans and, in those species with three bones in the pectoral girdle, the coracoid. Some mammalian species (e.g. the dog and the horse) have only the scapula. In humans, the only joints between the shoulder girdle and axial skeleton are the sternoclavicular joints on each side. No joint exists between each scapula and the rib cage; instead the muscular connection between the two permits relatively great mobility of the shoulder girdle in relation to the pelvic girdle. In those species having only the scapula, no joint exists between the forelimb and the thorax, the only attachment being muscular[WP]. Examples: There are only two instances, right and left pectoral girdle skeletons.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0008194.name: tibiotarsus
ref.uberon.UBERON_0008194.definition: The tibiotarsus is the large bone between the femur and the tarsometatarsus in the leg of a bird. It is the fusion of the proximal part of the tarsus with the tibia. A similar structure also occurred in the Mesozoic Heterodontosauridae. These small ornithischian dinosaurs were unrelated to birds and the similarity of their pes bones is best explained by convergent evolution.
ref.uberon.UBERON_0008194.notes: EXTRACTED: Uberon states it; not a creature part, not physically verified. Human anatomy is REFERENCE, never automatically Chimera proportions.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0008195.name: tarsometatarsus
ref.uberon.UBERON_0008195.definition: The tarsometatarsus is a bone that is found in the lower leg of certain tetrapods, namely birds. It is formed from the fusion of several bones found in other types of animals, and homologous to the mammalian tarsal (ankle) and metatarsal (pes) bones. Despite this, the tarsometatarsus of birds is often referred to as just the tarsus or metatarsus.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0008449.name: trochlear notch
ref.uberon.UBERON_0008449.definition: The semilunar notch of the ulna (trochlear notch of ulna, greater sigmoid cavity) is a large depression, formed by the olecranon and the coronoid process, and serving for articulation with the trochlea of the humerus. About the middle of either side of this notch is an indentation, which contracts it somewhat, and indicates the junction of the olecranon and the coronoid process. The notch is concave from above downward, and divided into a medial and a lateral portion by a smooth ridge running from the summit of the olecranon to the tip of the coronoid process. The medial portion is the larger, and is slightly concave transversely; the lateral is convex above, slightly concave below.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0009984.name: medial condyle of femur
ref.uberon.UBERON_0009984.definition: The medial condyle is one of the two projections on the lower extremity of femur. The medial condyle is larger than the lateral (outer) condyle due to more weight bearing caused by the center of gravity being medial to the knee. On the posterior surface of the condyle the linea aspera (a ridge running down the posterior shaft of the femur) turns into the medial supracondylar ridge. The outermost protrusion on the medial surface of the medial condyle is referred to as the 'medial epicondyle' and can be palpated by running fingers medially from the patella with the knee in flexion.
ref.uberon.UBERON_0009984.notes: EXTRACTED: Uberon states it; not a creature part, not physically verified. Human anatomy is REFERENCE, never automatically Chimera proportions.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0009985.name: lateral condyle of femur

ref.uberon.UBERON_0009986.name: lateral epicondyle of femur
ref.uberon.UBERON_0009986.definition: The lateral epicondyle of the femur, smaller and less prominent than the medial epicondyle, gives attachment to the fibular collateral ligament of the knee-joint. Directly below it is a small depression from which a smooth well-marked groove curves obliquely upward and backward to the posterior extremity of the condyle.
ref.uberon.UBERON_0009986.notes: EXTRACTED: Uberon states it; not a creature part, not physically verified. Human anatomy is REFERENCE, never automatically Chimera proportions.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0009987.name: medial epicondyle of femur
ref.uberon.UBERON_0009987.definition: The medial epicondyle of the femur is a bony protrusion located on the medial side of the bone's distal end. Located above the medial condyle, it bears an elevation, the adductor tubercle, which serves for the attachment of the superficial part, or 'tendinous insertion', of the adductor magnus. This tendinous part here forms an intermuscular septum which forms the medial separation between the thigh's flexors and extensors. Behind it, and proximally to the medial condyle is a rough impression which gives origin to the medial head of the Gastrocnemius.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0010544.name: metacarpus skeleton
ref.uberon.UBERON_0010544.definition: The metacarpus is the intermediate part of the manus skeleton that is located between the phalanges (bones of the fingers) distally and the carpus which forms the connection to the forearm. The metacarpus consists of metacarpal bones. The metacarpals form a transverse arch to which the rigid row of distal carpal bones are fixed. The peripheral metacarpals (those of the thumb and little finger) form the sides of the cup of the palmar gutter and as they are brought together they deepen this concavity. The index metacarpal is the most firmly fixed, while the thumb metacarpal articulates with the trapezium and acts independently from the others. The middle metacarpals are tightly united to the carpus by intrinsic interlocking bone elements at their bases. The ring metacarpal forms a transitional element of the semi-independent last metacarpal. [WP,unvetted].

ref.uberon.UBERON_0010746.definition: The extension of the ilium above the level of the acetabulum. Attachment site for both hindlimb and caudal musculature. Medially is the site of attachment of the sacral ribs, where these exist[PHENOSCAPE:ad].

ref.uberon.UBERON_0010747.name: body of ilium
ref.uberon.UBERON_0010747.definition: The body of ilium enters into the formation of the acetabulum, of which it forms rather less than two-fifths. Its external surface is partly articular, partly non-articular; the articular segment forms part of the lunate surface of the acetabulum, the non-articular portion contributes to the acetabular fossa. The internal surface of the body is part of the wall of the lesser pelvis and gives origin to some fibers of the Obturator internus. Below, it is continuous with the pelvic surfaces of the ischium and pubis, only a faint line indicating the place of union.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0011187.name: ventral tubercle of humerus
ref.uberon.UBERON_0011187.definition: The greater tubercle of the humerus is situated lateral to the head of the humerus and posteriolateral to the lesser tubercle. Its upper surface is rounded and marked by three flat impressions. the highest of these gives ('superior facet') insertion to the Supraspinatus the middle ('middle facet') to the Infraspinatus. the lowest one ('inferior facet'), and the body of the bone for about 2.5 cm. below it, to the Teres minor. The lateral surface of the greater tubercle is convex, rough, and continuous with the lateral surface of the body. Between the greater tubercle and the lesser tubercle is the intertubercular sulcus (bicipital groove).

ref.uberon.UBERON_0014442.name: superior ischial ramus
ref.uberon.UBERON_0014442.definition: The superior ramus of the ischium (descending ramus) projects downward and backward from the body and presents for examination three surfaces: external, internal, and posterior. The external surface is quadrilateral in shape. It is bounded above by a groove which lodges the tendon of the Obturator externus; below, it is continuous with the inferior ramus; in front it is limited by the posterior margin of the obturator foramen; behind, a prominent margin separates it from the posterior surface. In front of this margin the surface gives origin to the Quadratus femoris, and anterior to this to some of the fibers of origin of the Obturator externus; the lower part of the surface gives origin to part of the Adductor magnus. The internal surface forms part of the bony wall of the lesser pelvis. In front it is limited by the posterior margin of the obturator foramen. Below, it is bounded by a sharp ridge which gives attachment to a falciform prolongation of the sacrotuberous ligament, and, more anteriorly, gives origin to the Transversus perinC&i and Ischiocavernosus. Posteriorly the ramus forms a large swelling, the tuberosity of the ischium.
ref.uberon.UBERON_0014442.notes: EXTRACTED: Uberon states it; not a creature part, not physically verified. Human anatomy is REFERENCE, never automatically Chimera proportions.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0014443.name: inferior ischial ramus
ref.uberon.UBERON_0014443.definition: The Inferior Ramus of the ischium (ascending ramus) is the thin, flattened part of the ischium, which ascends from the superior ramus, and joins the inferior ramus of the pubisbthe junction being indicated in the adult by a raised line. The outer surface is uneven for the origin of the obturator externus and some of the fibers of the adductor magnus; its inner surface forms part of the anterior wall of the pelvis. Its medial border is thick, rough, slightly everted, forms part of the outlet of the pelvis, and presents two ridges and an intervening space. The ridges are continuous with similar ones on the inferior ramus of the pubis: to the outer is attached the deep layer of the superficial perineal fascia (fascia of Colles), and to the inner the inferior fascia of the urogenital diaphragm. If these two ridges be traced downward, they will be found to join with each other just behind the point of origin of the transversus perinC&i; here the two layers of fascia are continuous behind the posterior border of the muscle. To the intervening space, just in front of the point of junction of the ridges, the transversus perinC&i is attached, and in front of this a portion of the crus penis vel clitoridis and the ischiocavernosus. Its lateral border is thin and sharp, and forms part of the medial margin of the obturator foramen.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200005.name: acromial process of scapula
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200005.definition: A skeletal element projection forming the flattened lateral continuation of the scapular spine, overhanging the glenohumeral joint and articulating with the lateral end of the clavicle at the acromioclavicular joint; it provides attachment for the deltoid muscle anteriorly and the trapezius posteriorly.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200010.name: anterior gluteal line of ilium of os coxa
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200010.definition: A zone of bone organ forming a curved ridge on the gluteal surface of the ilium of the os coxa (innominate bone), running from the iliac crest toward the greater sciatic notch and separating the areas of origin of the gluteus medius superiorly from the gluteus minimus inferiorly.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200013.name: anterolateral tubercle of tibia
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200013.definition: A skeletal element projection situated on the anterolateral aspect of the proximal tibial epiphysis, just inferior to the lateral articular surface. It serves as an attachment site for the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus and elements of the anterolateral ligamentous complex of the knee.
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200013.notes: EXTRACTED: Uberon states it; not a creature part, not physically verified. Human anatomy is REFERENCE, never automatically Chimera proportions.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200014.name: arcuate line of ilium of os coxa
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200014.definition: A zone of bone organ forming a smooth, rounded ridge on the medial surface of the ilium of the os coxa (innominate bone), continuing the pelvic brim from the sacral promontory toward the iliopectineal eminence and demarcating the boundary between the greater and lesser pelvis.
